filo delete [DIR] [-y]
filo delete FILE [-y]

  Lists the files past their retention under DIR (inside a root), or under every
  root, whose content has not changed since the retention was set, then asks:
  all, select one by one, list them all, or none [a/s/l/N]. In a terminal the
  list shows 10 entries; l lists every one. Select goes file by file: d delete,
  r new retention, s skip or q quit. Enter, or an answer filo does not know,
  never deletes anything. Without a terminal it only lists. Deletion is
  permanent: there is no recycle bin, so keep backups.

Flags
  -y                       delete them all (or do all of the CSV) without asking

  Just before deleting, each file is read again. It is deleted only if it is
  still at its path as the same file and its content is still the content its
  retention was set on; otherwise it is skipped with one line saying why. A file
  that cannot be read is never deleted. Directories the run emptied are removed,
  up to the root. Exit code 1 if a file could not be read or deleted.

  A file kept until a date is past its retention on that date: kept until
  2026-12-31, it is listed from 2026-12-31 on. Nothing is deleted then; it is
  listed the next time filo delete runs.

  filo delete FILE carries out a duplicates CSV (filo export duplicates). Each
  group is checked against the disk: a group any of whose files changed or moved
  since the export is skipped, and a copy gone since is ignored. It lists what
  it will delete, what it will record (contents marked always, files kept as
  separate files) and what it won't touch, then asks: yes, select group by
  group, list, or no [y/s/l/N]. A copy is deleted only while a copy kept is
  still there with the same content, and only if a copy kept lasts at least as
  long (its keep_until). A CSV can be edited further and run again: groups done
  are reported, and only what is still as exported is acted on. Exit code 1 if
  the CSV refuses a group.
